title: Pictures That Talk
bigQuestion: How can a picture tell us something without any words?

story.title: The Picture on the Old Building
story.kicker: Maya sees a carved picture high on an old building. What is it trying to say?
paragraphs: Maya walks downtown with her grandpa. The buildings are tall and old. Maya looks up. High on one stone wall, she sees a carved picture. It has two tools that cross.
One tool looks like a big letter L. The other tool has two long legs, like an upside-down V. Maya pulls Grandpa's sleeve. "What does that picture mean?" she asks.
Grandpa smiles. "That is a symbol," he says. "It stands for builders. A club of people called Freemasons uses it. They met in this building long ago."
Maya looks again. The picture has no words. But now it tells her something. "Pictures can talk!" she says. Grandpa laughs. "Yes. You just have to learn how to listen."
story.think: Have you seen a picture on a wall or a sign that made you wonder what it meant? What did you think it said?

lessons.title: A Picture Means an Idea
lessons.mainIdea: A symbol is a picture that stands for an idea.
reading: Sam draws a red heart on a card for his mom. The heart does not say any words. But Mom knows what it means. It means "I love you."
A *symbol* is a picture that stands for an idea. A heart stands for love. A smiley face stands for happy. A star can stand for a great job.
You see symbols every day. You see them on doors, on boxes, and on screens. When you know the idea, you can read the picture.

words.d: a picture or shape that stands for an idea

look.title: Three Pictures on a Card
look.text: Look at the card on the table. In one corner is a red heart. In the middle is a big yellow smiley face. At the bottom is a gold star.
look.prompt: Say what each picture means. Which one would you put on a card for a friend?

check.q: What is a symbol?
choices: A picture that stands for an idea
A long word with many letters
A sound that a dog makes
check.why: The reading says a symbol is a picture that stands for an idea.

check.q: What does the red heart on Sam's card mean?
check.why: Sam's mom knows the heart means "I love you."

check.q: What can a star stand for?
check.why: The reading says a star can stand for a great job.

lessons.title: Signs on the Road
lessons.mainIdea: Road signs use shapes and colors so people can read them fast.
reading: Lee rides in the car with his dad. They come to a red sign with eight sides. Dad stops the car. The sign did not need to say a lot. Its shape and color told Dad what to do.
A *sign* is a board that gives a message. A stop sign is red. It has eight sides. No other road sign has that shape. So drivers know it fast, even from far away.
A yield sign has three sides. It means slow down and let others go first. A school sign has five sides. It means children may be near.

words.d: a board with a picture, shape or words that gives a message

look.title: How Many Sides?
look.cite: Federal Highway Administration, Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices, 2009 edition
look.prompt: Which sign has the most sides? Draw that shape in the air with your finger.

check.q: How many sides does a stop sign have?
check.why: A stop sign is red and has eight sides.

check.q: What does a yield sign tell a driver?
choices: Slow down and let others go first
check.why: The reading says a yield sign means slow down and let others go first.

check.q: Why can drivers know a stop sign fast?
choices: Its shape and color are special
check.why: The stop sign is red with eight sides. No other road sign has that shape.

lessons.title: A Floor With Seven Steps
lessons.mainIdea: Long ago, a group in Italy put seven pictures on a floor to show seven steps.
reading: Ostia is an old town in Italy, near the sea. Long ago, a group met there. That was more than 1,700 years ago. They put a picture floor in their hallway. It is made of tiny stones.
The floor has seven pictures in a row, like a *ladder*. Each picture is one step. New members started on the first step. They could climb higher over time.
The first step was called the Raven. A raven is a big black bird. The top step was called the Father. The floor shows the whole ladder with no words needed.

words.d: steps that go up, one after another
a picture made from many tiny pieces of stone or glass

look.title: The Floor at Ostia
look.text: A hallway floor in Ostia, Italy, is a mosaic in seven panels, one for each step of the group. Each panel has its own pictures and a planet. One more panel shows the name Felicissimus. Diggers found it in 1940.
look.cite: Mithraeum.eu, entry on the Mithraeum of Felicissimus, Ostia; Parco archeologico di Ostia antica, educational panel "Mitreo di Felicissimo"
look.prompt: How many steps does the floor show? Why might a group show its steps in pictures?

check.q: In which country is the old town of Ostia?
check.why: The reading says Ostia is an old town in Italy, near the sea.

check.q: How many pictures are in the ladder on the floor?
check.why: The floor has seven pictures in a row. Each one is a step.

check.q: What was the first step called?
check.why: The first step was the Raven. The top step was the Father.

lessons.title: The Builders' Two Tools
lessons.mainIdea: The square and compass are real builders' tools, and Freemasons use them as a symbol.
reading: Pat builds a birdhouse. She uses a *square* to make each corner just right. The square is shaped like a big letter L.
She uses a *compass* to draw a perfect circle for the door. A compass has two legs. One leg stays still. The other leg turns around it.
Long ago, stone builders used these same tools. A club called the Freemasons began with builders. Today Freemasons still use the square and compass as their symbol.

words.d: a builder's tool shaped like an L, used to make straight corners
a tool with two legs, used to draw circles

look.title: Two Tools That Cross
look.text: Look at the picture carved in the stone. An L-shaped square points down. A compass with two long legs points up. The two tools cross in the middle, like a diamond.
look.prompt: Which tool makes corners? Which tool draws circles? Show each shape with your hands.

check.q: What does a compass help you draw?
check.why: Pat uses a compass to draw a perfect circle.

check.q: What shape is a builder's square?
check.why: The reading says the square is shaped like a big letter L.

check.q: Which club uses the square and compass as its symbol?
check.why: Freemasons began with builders. They still use these tools as their symbol.

lessons.title: Reading Old Buildings
lessons.mainIdea: Carvings on old buildings can tell us who built or used them.
reading: Jin looks at his school door. Above it, carved in stone, is an open book. The book tells people that this is a place to learn.
Old buildings often have *carvings*. A carving is a picture cut into stone or wood. Some carvings show the group that built or used the building.
See a square and compass? Freemasons may have met there. You can be a symbol detective. Look up, look close, and ask what the picture says.

words.d: a picture cut into stone or wood

look.title: Look Up on Your Street
look.text: Picture a walk on your street. Look up above the doors. One door has a stone book. One has a bell. One has two crossing tools, a square and a compass.
look.prompt: Pick one carving. What could it tell you about the building?

check.q: What is a carving?
choices: A picture cut into stone or wood
check.why: The reading says a carving is a picture cut into stone or wood.

check.q: What does the open book over Jin's school door tell people?
choices: This is a place to learn
check.why: The book tells people the building is a place to learn.

check.q: What can a square and compass on a wall mean?
check.why: The reading says a square and compass can mean Freemasons met in the building.

lessons.title: Badges, Pins and Flags
lessons.mainIdea: Badges, pins and flags show which group you belong to.
reading: Rosa wears a small pin shaped like a leaf. Her friend has the same pin. They are both in the garden club. The pin shows they belong together.
A *badge* is a small sign you wear to show your group. Scouts wear badges. Team players wear the same colors. Long ago, many clubs had their own badges and pins.
A *flag* shows a group too. The flag of the United States has 50 stars and 13 stripes. Each star stands for one state. Illinois is one of those stars.

words.d: a small sign you wear to show a group you belong to
a piece of cloth with colors and pictures that stand for a group or place

look.title: Count the U.S. Flag
look.cite: United States Code, Title 4, Section 1 (the flag: 13 stripes, a star for each state)
look.prompt: Which number is the biggest? What does each star stand for?

check.q: Why do Rosa and her friend wear the same leaf pin?
choices: They are in the garden club
check.why: The pin shows they belong to the same garden club.

check.q: How many stars are on the flag of the United States?
check.why: The flag has 50 stars, one for each state. It has 13 stripes.

check.q: What is a badge?
choices: A small sign you wear to show your group
check.why: The reading says a badge is a small sign you wear to show your group.

lessons.title: Make a Class Symbol
lessons.mainIdea: A class can make its own symbol to show what it cares about.
reading: Room 12 wants a symbol. First, they talk. They love to read. They love to help. They ask, what picture could show both ideas?
Mia draws a book. Omar draws two hands. The class puts them together: two hands holding a book. Now they have a class symbol. It is their own *design*.
A good symbol is simple. It is easy to draw and easy to see. It shows an idea the group shares. Everyone can help make it.

words.d: a plan or drawing you make for something new

look.title: Plan Your Class Symbol
look.text: Step 1: Say one thing your class loves. Step 2: Think of a picture for it. Step 3: Draw it big and simple. Step 4: Share it and add a friend's idea.
look.prompt: What does your class love? Draw a simple picture that shows it.

check.q: What did Room 12 put together for its symbol?
check.why: Mia drew a book and Omar drew two hands. The class put them together.

check.q: What makes a good symbol?
choices: It is simple and easy to see
Only one person can draw it
check.why: The reading says a good symbol is simple, easy to draw and easy to see.

check.q: What did Room 12 do first?
choices: They talked about what they love
check.why: First, the class talked. They love to read and to help.

review.q: A picture that stands for an idea is called a what?
review.why: A symbol is a picture that stands for an idea, like a heart for love.

review.q: Which road sign has eight sides?
review.why: The stop sign is red and has eight sides.

review.q: What does the old floor in Ostia show?
review.why: The floor in Ostia shows seven pictures, one for each step of the group.

review.q: Which tool has two legs and draws circles?
review.why: A compass has two legs. One stays still and one turns to draw a circle.

review.q: What does a badge or pin show?
review.why: Badges and pins show which group you belong to, like Rosa's garden club pin.

review.q: Maya sees a square and compass on an old building. What can it tell her?
review.why: Grandpa says the square and compass stand for builders and the Freemasons, who met there.
